// Projects

Featured Projects

Robotics · Fabrication

Circuit Launch Coffee Robot

Improved the mechanical design of a coffee-serving robot as part of the Circuit Launch Makerspace Pilot Education Program in Oakland, CA. Used Agile/Kanban methodology to track progress with a cohort of students. Modeled a servo-motor-driven robot arm in SOLIDWORKS with full drawing files for each part, then fabricated the base and joints using a laser cutter and 3D printer.

SOLIDWORKS Servo Motor Laser Cutting 3D Printing Kanban

Medical Device · Testing

Therapeutic Hand Device with Tensioner System

Designed a therapeutic glove for a user with left-hand muscle impairment, completed for a senior mechanical engineering design class at CSUS. Modeled the glove frame and tensioners in SolidWorks with adjustable attachment sites. Validated PLA material using the SATEC Tensile Test Machine on 6 rectangular test members — breaking load: 1,066 lbf. The finished prototype supports up to 11 lbs in tension for repetitive therapeutic hand exercises targeting flexor and extensor finger muscles.

SOLIDWORKS PLA / FDM Tensile Testing

Mechatronics · Biomedical

Assistive Glove with Biofeedback System

M.S. capstone project and 1st Place WE19 Conference winner. An assistive hand device for post-stroke users with limited finger extensor movement, detecting metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint angles while providing visual LED biofeedback. The device allows users with spasticity to independently don, use, and remove it. An Arduino program records MCP joint angles by using a flex-sensor voltage divider circuit mapped from 0–180°, logging data via PLX-DAQ software and MATLAB. Validated with static (electrogoniometer comparison) and dynamic tests using the Sollerman Hand Function protocol — transverse volar grip, spherical volar grip, and pulp pinch.

// Testing & Validation

1 Static Validation

Used to quantitatively test the repeatability of angle measurements provided by the flex sensors. Readings of voltage, resistance, and bend angle were compared against values measured by an electrogoniometer.

2 Dynamic Validation

An Arduino Uno and MATLAB program recorded flex sensor data for each finger, outputting graphs of bend angle vs. time. Validated using the Sollerman Hand Function test — transverse volar grip, spherical volar grip, and pulp pinch.

📊 Results — Transverse Volar Grip Run 2

Degree of angle measurement (pinky, ring, middle, and index fingers) plotted vs. normalized time in seconds for one run of the transverse volar grip test.

// Design

1 Ring Clip

Serves as attachment sites for flex sensors. Adjustable to fit most finger sizes — flex sensors are placed in a fabric sleeve and attached via Velcro for adjustability.

2a Housing

Holds the microcontroller and provides placement for flex sensors attached via Velcro. Made from PLA for low cost and high durability.

2b Lid

Contains holes for LEDs and slots for wires from the flex sensor to feed into the microcontroller. Secured to housing with screws.

3 Light Emitting Diode (LED)

Provides visual biofeedback to detect finger angle changes during exercise. Three LEDs light up at intensities corresponding to a percentage of the target angle reached.

4 Microcontroller

An Arduino Uno housed inside the device, used to record data from the flex sensors for each respective finger.

5 Flex Sensor

Used for their low cost and ability to record finger joint range of motion. Wired to the analog input of the microcontroller to record MCP joint angles.

Arduino MATLAB PLX-DAQ Flex Sensors PLA / FDM Sewing
